hints: Find the centre $M$ of the square as the midpoint of $AC$: $M = \left(\dfrac{1 + 7}{2}, \dfrac{2 + 10}{2}\right) = (4, 6)$.
For a square of diagonal $d$, the area is $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} d^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 100 = 50$.
walkthrough:
A square has equal perpendicular diagonals; its area is half their product.
Calculate the centre $M$ as the midpoint of diagonal $AC$:
$$M = \left(\dfrac{1 + 7}{2}, \dfrac{2 + 10}{2}\right) = (4, 6)$$

Calculate the squared diagonal length and the area of the square:
$$AC^2 = (7 - 1)^2 + (10 - 2)^2 = 36 + 64 = 100$$
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times AC^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 100 = 50$$
